long_biography.plain_text:
A failed construction venture redirected Mohammed Al Barwani towards the oil expertise he had acquired during a decade at Petroleum Development Oman. He began MB Group's oilfield business with manpower supply and equipment ordered against customer contracts, keeping costs low until banks financed larger purchases against service work. Acquiring a marginal Omani oilfield then gave the group its entry into exploration and production.

Al Barwani later extended acquisition-led growth across several countries while keeping governance within the family. His wife managed administration, finance, human resources and legal work while he led technical operations. Their five children received shares early and took roles across the group, supported by written family protocols intended to prepare later generations for ownership and management.
